title: C1785 — Driver-side hood hinge connector
introduction:
The title gets me to the hood hinge; the Function column explains the electrical company it keeps. This reference maps the driver-side hinge connector to the left-hand pedestrian-impact hood actuator connections. Start by confirming CNumber and Description, then match the drawing's cavity labels to the assignment rows.

Read the positive and negative function labels as a pair associated with that actuator. Neither label alone establishes a battery-feed connection or a chassis-ground connection. Circuit Number, Color, Gauge and Terminal Part Number keep each connection's identity together. The pigtail section then links the connector's housing identity to the listed service assembly.

This is a connector-reading guide. It supplies no actuator handling sequence, physical viewing direction, access, probing, energizing or replacement procedure. Gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used are also unspecified here. Keep the recorded entries intact and use the applicable service procedure before handling or testing the actuator system.

edits.why: I recognize this illustration by its rounded rectangular face, vertically stacked circular cavities, tall rectangular feature above the face and projection to the left as drawn. These features help locate the cavity labels on the page. They do not establish a release movement, an installed orientation or a physical probing direction.

Cavity connects the drawing to its corresponding circuit row. Read each row through Function to preserve the actuator's positive or negative designation, then retain its circuit identity, color, gauge and terminal reference together. The negative designation is an actuator connection label; treating it as a chassis-ground instruction would go beyond this map.

Engineering Shell relates this service entry to the housing identity, while Number and Service Part provide distinct catalog references. Gauge, Material and Cavities describe the pigtail entry. I keep those fields separate from the actuator circuit rows; the parts lookup does not establish a splice method, replacement sequence or actuator service setup.
